findings.issue_text: Backup code single-use enforcement in next-auth-options.ts:~145 is not atomic: code checked with indexOf and invalidated via a separate prisma.user.update, so two concurrent logins with the same backup code can both pass verification
TOTP setup endpoint regenerates and overwrites backupCodes unconditionally, silently invalidating previously issued codes for users who already enabled 2FA and re-run setup
disable.ts:46 backup code path has no attempt limiting/throttling on backup code guesses, enabling brute-force attempts against the 10-hex-char space
disable.ts:46 backup code only verifies membership and relies on a later backupCodes: null write; if any step fails after a correct backup code is submitted the code remains valid

EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: backup codes are generated and persisted in the setup step but only displayed after the enable step; cancelling between setup and enable leaves stored codes the user never sees, and a later re-run shows different codes causing confusion
BackupCode.tsx default export is named TwoFactor, which is misleading in React DevTools/error traces; should be named BackupCode

Backup code comparison is case-sensitive (backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))) while codes are lowercase hex; uppercase input from autocapitalization causes valid codes to be rejected; no case normalization on client or server

Zero tests for core backup code flows: login with backup code, single-use consumption, disabling 2FA with backup code, and incorrect/missing code error paths; only download/copy/close buttons are exercised

EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: useState([]) leaves backupCodes typed as never[], so backupCodes.map((code) => ...) and formatBackupCode(code: string) should fail type checking; needs explicit useState<string[]>([])
Locale string "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings but no UI exists to regenerate backup codes for accounts with 2FA already enabled, making the instruction unactionable

disable.ts:49 throws new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) on missing encryption key producing an unhandled 500, inconsistent with structured res.status(400).json({ error: ... }) responses in other failure paths (same pattern in next-auth-options.ts)

Used backup codes are replaced with null and re-encrypted rather than removed, so the all-codes-used state is never detected or surfaced; login UI keeps offering the backup-code path when no codes remain, yielding only a generic incorrect error

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOTP setup endpoint regenerates and overwrites backupCodes unconditionally, silently invalidating previously issued codes for users who already enabled 2FA and re-run setup

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup handler always generates new `backupCodes` and persists them via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: ... } })` with no check for an existing enabled 2FA state. So re-running setup would overwrite any previously stored backup codes. However, this mirrors existing setup behavior that already overwrites the TOTP secret / resets `twoFactorEnabled: false`, so “invalidating previous codes” is an expected consequence of restarting 2FA setup rather than a new standalone correctness defect. The main review concern is guarding/UX around regenerating and persisting new backup codes during setup (potentially before the user completes enable and records them), not that the overwrite occurs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disable.ts:46 backup code path has no attempt limiting/throttling on backup code guesses, enabling brute-force attempts against the 10-hex-char space

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` validates a user-supplied backup code via plaintext comparison after decrypting stored codes, but the handler shows no throttling/rate-limiting/lockout logic around repeated failed guesses (unlike other auth flows elsewhere that may use rate-limit helpers). This introduces a brute-forceable online verification endpoint for backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disable.ts:46 backup code only verifies membership and relies on a later backupCodes: null write; if any step fails after a correct backup code is submitted the code remains valid

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code path only checks that `req.body.backupCode` exists in the decrypted list (`indexOf(...)`) and then relies on the final Prisma update (`data: { backupCodes: null, twoFactorEnabled: false, ... }`) to invalidate codes. It does not remove/mark the specific backup code as used when it’s accepted (unlike the login flow in `next-auth-options.ts`, which nulls the used entry and re-encrypts). If the request errors after backup-code verification but before the final write (e.g., DB failure), the same backup code would remain usable on retry. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/atomicity concern, but it’s not clearly a user-visible or security defect given that no state change occurred unless the disable succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: backup codes are generated and persisted in the setup step but only displayed after the enable step; cancelling between setup and enable leaves stored codes the user never sees, and a later re-run shows different codes causing confusion

adjudication.rationale: In `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated and persisted immediately during the setup call (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)`) even though `twoFactorEnabled` remains `false`. In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, those codes are only shown in the later `DisplayBackupCodes` step, which is reached only after `handleEnable` succeeds (`setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)`). Because the modal shows a Cancel button for all steps except `DisplayBackupCodes`, the user can cancel after setup (QR displayed / before enable), leaving persisted backup codes they never saw; re-running setup will generate/store a new set, making the previously stored set unknown to the user and potentially confusing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zero tests for core backup code flows: login with backup code, single-use consumption, disabling 2FA with backup code, and incorrect/missing code error paths; only download/copy/close buttons are exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new backup-code logic and error paths (e.g., login authorize() handling of `credentials.backupCode` with consumption/re-encryption in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, disable via backup code in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, and new ErrorCodes/messages), but the only added Playwright coverage is for the backup-codes UI buttons (download/copy/close) in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`. The test file even notes `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`, confirming missing coverage for core flows like login via backup code, single-use behavior, disabling 2FA via backup code, and incorrect/missing-code errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: useState([]) leaves backupCodes typed as never[], so backupCodes.map((code) => ...) and formatBackupCode(code: string) should fail type checking; needs explicit useState<string[]>([])

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx the state is initialized as `const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState([]);`, which infers `never[]` in many TS setups, but this does not necessarily cause a type-check failure in the shown diff: `response.json()` is `any`, so `setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes)` is accepted, and mapping over `never[]` plus calling `formatBackupCode(code)` doesn’t inherently error because `never` is assignable to `string` (and `backupCodes.map(...)` is valid). The finding claims this 'should fail type checking', which is not verifiably true from the diff alone. Explicitly typing `useState<string[]>([])` would improve type safety, but the stated failure is not demonstrated by this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Locale string "missing_backup_codes" tells users to generate codes in settings but no UI exists to regenerate backup codes for accounts with 2FA already enabled, making the instruction unactionable

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new nullable `backupCodes` column (migration + schema) but does not backfill it for existing users with `twoFactorEnabled=true`. Both login (`next-auth-options.ts`) and disable endpoint (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) can now return `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` when a user tries the new “Lost access” backup-code flow (login.tsx / DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx). The locale string `missing_backup_codes` instructs users to generate codes in settings, but this PR only generates backup codes during `/totp/setup` (EnableTwoFactorModal flow) and provides no UI/endpoint to regenerate backup codes for already-enabled 2FA accounts. For users who lost their TOTP and have no backup codes (likely after migration), the instruction is unactionable and they remain locked out of the backup-code recovery path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disable.ts:49 throws new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) on missing encryption key producing an unhandled 500, inconsistent with structured res.status(400).json({ error: ... }) responses in other failure paths (same pattern in next-auth-options.ts)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing, while all other validation failures return structured `res.status(400).json({ error: ... })`. Nothing in the shown diff indicates this throw is caught, so it will result in a generic/unstructured 500 response, inconsistent with the endpoint’s other error paths. The same missing-key throw pattern also appears in `next-auth-options.ts` (there it’s within `authorize`, where throwing is the normal error mechanism), but in this API route it’s a behavior/response-format regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Used backup codes are replaced with null and re-encrypted rather than removed, so the all-codes-used state is never detected or surfaced; login UI keeps offering the backup-code path when no codes remain, yielding only a generic incorrect error

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, verified backup codes are marked as used by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting the full array, but there is no subsequent check for an “all codes used” condition (i.e., array contains only nulls) to trigger `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes`. As a result, once all codes are consumed, future attempts will always hit `indexOf(...) === -1` and throw `IncorrectBackupCode`, even though the real state is “no backup codes remain.” The login UI also unconditionally exposes the backup-code path via the `lost_access` toggle without checking availability, so users can keep selecting it even when no valid codes exist.
